action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's call is to scale up the acquisition budget: the longer-term trend and the last three months both still lean up, with medium confidence (66/100 after today's news, 62 on market data alone), so this remains a reasonable time to fund growth, weighted toward channels that bring active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price has just slipped below its 50-day average ($81,823) and the Fed decides on rates on 28 October, add budget in small steps and keep part of it flexible, ready to pause if price keeps sliding toward $74,972 (where a drop signal would start). This is a budget posture based on trailing data, not a price call or trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still leans up, but this week Bitcoin is under some pressure and has slipped just below a line that matters. Short term, the mood leans mildly down: price is about $80,900, down slightly over the week, and US Bitcoin funds just had their largest one-day outflow since June (about $635M on Thursday, per The Block via PANews). News is taking a little more off the mood, mainly an attack that forced the Initia blockchain to pause and spreading worries about AI-company debt (both PANews). If price closes above $81,823 (the 50-day average) the short term turns clearly up; below $72,906 (the 200-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days, which suits a calm, explain-the-news tone rather than hype.

Over the next month, the picture still leans moderately up. Price is about 24% higher than three months ago and about 74% of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, but it now sits just under the 50-day average. Price first needs to win back $81,823 (the 50-day average); above $86,603 (the 90-day high) there is room to climb. The Fed's rate decision on 28 October is the next scheduled event: reclaiming the 50-day line after it would keep growth campaigns well timed, while staying below would argue for adding new spend more slowly.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 11% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about a third below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a mature uptrend. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,906 (the 200-day average), with $66,860 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. News is adding a little here, with HSBC launching a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin in its PayMe app and Mastercard settling payments in USDC (both PANews); a faster-rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and support steady spending on new users.
